syllabusTopics: Limits and continuity: limits of a function, indeterminate forms, algebraic properties of limits (without proof), basic theorems on limits of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Continuity of a function, types of discontinuity, graphs of discontinuous function
Derivatives: derivative of a function, derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions by definition (simple forms)
Rules of differentiation; derivatives of parametric and implicit functions; higher order derivatives
Geometric interpretation of derivative; monotonicity of a function, interval of monotonicity, extreme values of a function, concavity, points of inflection
Anti-derivatives: integration using basic integrals, integration by substitution and by parts methods
The definite integral; the definite integral as an area under the given curve; area between two curves

card.title: Limits: Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential and Logarithmic

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Four families, one architecture: algebraic stars from difference-of-powers identities, trigonometric stars from radian geometry, exponential and logarithmic stars from e's self-replication, all composed through u → 0 and steered by manufactured denominators. Same-order contestants leave coefficient ratios; the growth ladder (ln < power < exponential < super-exponential) decides mixed-family races at infinity.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Using the standard limits with x in degrees, which changes every value by a factor involving $\pi$.  ·  Applying $\lim \ln f = \ln(\lim f)$ when the limit of $f$ is negative, where the logarithm is not defined at all.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Where a formula is quoted it is valid only under the conditions stated; Using the standard limits with x in degrees, which changes every value by a factor involving $\pi$.  ·  Every result here follows from the definitions, so a first-principles derivation is always a valid fallback in the exam.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Steering in action*** - (sin 5x)/x = 5(sin 5x)/(5x) -> 5: the inserted 5x is the star's demanded denominator, the outside 5 pays for it.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Diagnose the family first; the family names the star; the star names the steering.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (5m): Evaluate lim_{x→0} (tan 4x − sin 2x)/(3x).** — **Split legally** (both pieces' limits exist): = lim (tan 4x)/(3x) − lim (sin 2x)/(3x). **First piece (star tan u/u, u = 4x):** (4/3)·(tan 4x)/(4x) → 4/3. **Second piece (star sin u/u, u = 2x):** (2/3)·(sin 2x)/(2x) → 2/3.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Evaluate lim_{x→0} (1 − cos 2x)/(x·tan 3x).** — **Order diagnosis:** 1 − cos 2x ~ (2x)²/2 = 2x² (order 2); x·tan 3x ~ 3x² (order 2) ⟹ same order ⟹ ratio of coefficients 2/3. **Rigorous:** [(1 − cos 2x)/(2x)²]·[(2x)²/(x·tan 3x)] = [1/2]·[4x²/(3x²)]·[(tan 3x)/(3x)]^{-1} → (1/2)(4/3)(1) = **2/3** ✓.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Annotating which star and which u is the working - the arithmetic is bookkeeping.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Every star is a first-order approximation; same-order contestants leave coefficient ratios.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Algebraic stars: (x^n - a^n)/(x-a) -> n a^(n-1); degree rules at infinity. Trig stars (radians): sin u/u -> 1, tan u/u -> 1, (1-cos u)/u -> 0, (1-cos u)/u^2 -> 1/2. Exp/log stars: (e^u - 1)/u -> 1, ln(1+u)/u -> 1, a^u - 1 ~ u ln a, (1+u)^(1/u) -> e.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The star table plus the growth ladder resolves every standard limit in the syllabus.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (6m): Evaluate lim_{x→∞} (ln(2x + 1))/(e^{3x} − 1)... interpreted as lim_{x→∞} ln(2x+1)/(e^{3x} − 1).** — **Identify the race:** log (bottom rung) vs exponential (top rung) — the ladder says the exponential dominates overwhelmingly.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Evaluate lim_{x→0} (2^x − 1)/(√(1 + x) − 1).** — **Form:** (1 − 1)/(1 − 1) = **0/0** ✓. **Numerator (general-base star):** 2ˣ − 1 ~ x·ln 2 ⟹ (2ˣ − 1)/x → **ln 2**.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Companion Doorway to the Four Families This canonical is the **short-form doorway** to limits of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions: the stars of each family and the steering craft in one page.…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Algebraic stars:** (xⁿ − aⁿ)/(x − a) → naⁿ⁻¹; (1 − cos u)/u² → 1/2; degree rules at ∞. - **Trigonometric stars (radians only):** sin u/u → 1; tan u/u → 1; (1 − cos u)/u → 0. - **Exponential/log stars:** (eᵘ − 1)/u → 1; ln(1 + u)/u → 1; aᵘ − 1 ~ u·ln a; (1 + u)^{1/u} → e.…  ·  ## 3. Deep Conceptual — Stars Are First-Order Taylor Approximations - Each star says a complicated function **agrees with a line (or a parabola) near its anchor**: sin u ~ u, eᵘ − 1 ~ u, ln(1+u) ~ u are all "slope = 1 at the anchor" statements; 1 − cos u ~ u²/2 is the parabolic correction. The star table is a table of local linearisations.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: NEB-style practice beyond the verified PYQs recorded on the parent canonicals.  ·  Match the star's form exactly, annotate u, verify u approaches its anchor.  ·  Evaluate lim_{x→0} (tan 4x)/(2x).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Evaluate lim_{x→0} (e^{5x} − 1)/(3x).  ·  Evaluate lim_{x→∞} (1 + 2/x)^{3x}.  ·  ## 4. Deep Conceptual — The Growth Ladder Across Families - At infinity the families race in a fixed order: **ln x < xᵖ < aˣ < xˣ**. Any higher rung dominates: x¹⁰⁰/eˣ → 0, ln(xⁿ)/x → 0, eˣ/xᵏ → ∞ — regardless of coefficients.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 5. Worked Example Types - **Type A — steer to sin u/u:** (sin 5x)/x = 5·(sin 5x)/(5x) → 5. - **Type B — second-order matching:** (1 − cos 4x)/x² = 16·(1 − cos 4x)/(4x)² → 16·(1/2) = 8. - **Type C — mixed exp/log:** (e^{3x} − 1)/ln(1 + 2x) → 3/2 by coefficient ratio.…  ·  ## 6.
